faqs.q: How do I choose the right size pétanque boule?
faqs.a: Pick a boule that sits comfortably in your palm with your fingers wrapped around it. Your hand size and whether you mostly point or shoot are the two main things to consider.

faqs.q: Do I need competition boules to play pétanque?
faqs.a: Only if you play in official competitions, which require approved boules. For the garden or the beach, a leisure set works fine.

faqs.q: What's the difference between boules for pointing and shooting?
faqs.a: Pointers often prefer smaller, heavier boules that stay put, while shooters often prefer larger, lighter boules that are easier to throw hard. Personal feel matters most, so try a few if you can.

endings.title: A leisure set for fun 🏖️
endings.bodyMd: For garden, beach and park games you don't need competition boules. A leisure set in a carry bag with a jack and a measuring tape is ideal, and lighter sets are easier for children and older players to throw.

endings.title: Competition boules for pointing 🎯
endings.bodyMd: Pointers often choose a slightly smaller, heavier boule that stays where it lands, with grooves for a sure grip. We'll suggest competition-approved sets in the size that fits your hand.

endings.title: Competition boules for shooting 💥
endings.bodyMd: Shooters often prefer a slightly larger, lighter boule that is easier to throw hard and accurately. We'll suggest competition-approved sets that suit your hand and the grip you like.

endings.title: An all-round competition set ⚖️
endings.bodyMd: If you point and shoot, a mid-weight boule in a size that fits your hand is the safe choice. It won't be the specialist's pick for either role, but it lets you play both without switching sets.
